newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans cap on banks' consumer lending.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans cap on banks' consumer lending.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said on Tuesday the bank was studying the possibility of putting a limit on local banks' exposure to consumer loans.
"We're still studying it. It could be a 20 to 30 percent cap," Reyes told reporters.
The decision follows the financial crisis which hit thrift bank, Monte de Piedad & Savings Bank, after it was discovered to have 1.8 billion pesos in bad loans mainly to small borrowers.
Some 55 percent of its loans were to tricycle taxi drivers.
"We don't usually impose such restrictions since we may be penalising banks with niche marketing strategies, but we should ensure that prudential limits are in place," he said.
Reyes said only a few banks have exceeded the 30 percent level at the moment.
In late April, the Central Bank imposed a similar limit on banks' exposure to real estate. Banks cannot make more than 20 percent of their loans to the property sector.
